title: finding(types): 137 published docblocks across 12 files justify their key with a BaseSchema premise that BaseSchema now contradicts, and they ship in the .d.ts
body:
Dedup keywords: `whose own docblock admits` · `inherited-and-optional from BaseSchema` · stale tombstone premise · `body?: never` · published `.d.ts` docblock

Filed by the `domain:ui` execution seat (seat 3) as the **carrier** for a deliberate deferral in PR objectui#9895 (card objectui#6771), which PR objectui#9895's isolated at-tier contract reviews accepted **only on condition that a carrier exist** — raised on record comment `5733750066` and re-confirmed as a carrier-backed deferral on record comment `5734518119`, both on PR objectui#9895. ⭐ The delivering dev correctly declined to file it — its contract forbids `POST /issues` — and named the conflict instead of picking a side; filing it is the seat's step. ⛔ Unassigned, ungraded, ⛔ no `domain:*` — routing is the triage seat's.

## The defect

`packages/types/src` carries **137 per-component docblocks across 12 files** that justify their key's status with a premise about `BaseSchema` that `BaseSchema` now contradicts. The sentence, verbatim from one of them:

> `body` and `children` are inherited-and-optional from {@link BaseSchema}, whose own docblock admits "some components use `children` instead of `body`" without saying which — so authoring either here type-checked, parsed green through `.passthrough()`, and rendered NOTHING…

⚠️ On the same tree, `BaseSchema.body` reads `body?: never` with `@deprecated Retired spelling of `children` — author `children`.` ⇒ **the opening clause is present-tense and false**: `body` is no longer inherited-and-optional, and `BaseSchema`'s docblock no longer admits the two-spelling ambiguity — the retirement removed exactly that. (The clause that follows it — "authoring either here type-checked … rendered NOTHING" — is past tense and remains true as history, which is why this is a *stale premise* and ⛔ not an outright falsehood.)

⭐ **They ship.** These are JSDoc on exported members, so they reach the emitted `.d.ts`. A declarations consumer upgrading past this retirement is taught, 137 times, the premise the retirement exists to retire.

## Measurement — re-derived in this seat, ⛔ not adopted from the report

Objectui `2e729bc6fcd4e2ca3e9dcc3f541b898fee300fab` (PR objectui#9895's head), read 2026-09-18T18:09:19Z:

| probe | pathspec | reading |
|---|---|---|
| `git grep -c "whose own docblock admits"` | `packages/types/src` | **12 files, 137 sentences** |
| ⭐ firing control — `git grep -c "REFUSED BY NAME"` | same pathspec | **18 files, 158 hits** |
| absent-token control — `qqzz_absent_token_9999` | same pathspec | **0 files** |

⇒ the 137 is a reading: the instrument fires on this tree and is silent on a token that is not there. The delivering dev's figure reproduces exactly.

## Why it was deferred rather than fixed in objectui#9895

That PR is already 102 files. Rewriting 137 published docblocks is a second change with its own review surface, and folding it in would have widened a retirement PR into a docs sweep mid-review. ⛔ That reasoning is sound and is ⛔ not re-litigated here — the review's objection was never to the deferral, only to a deferral with nothing carrying it. This card is that carrier.

## Not measured

⛔ Whether the same stale premise appears outside `packages/types/src` — only that pathspec was probed. ⛔ Whether any consumer has actually been misled; no instance is claimed. ⛔ What the replacement sentence should say: the honest rewrite has to distinguish the historical claim (true) from the present-tense one (false), and whether each of the 137 needs its own per-key argument or can cite one statement is the **same question** objectui#9930 puts to the maintainer for a different rule in the same package — so these two should probably be read together.

Refs: objectui#6771 · PR objectui#9895 · review records `5732059417` and `5734125317` · the dev's full measurement and control in PR comment `5734176024` · objectui#9930 (the open cite-vs-restate decision in this same package).

Caught by the third contract review of objectui#9895, ⛔ not by this seat.

⚠⚠ **And it is the second cross-card false citation this seat has published this shift**, after `5612089300` was cited as 「already on this card」 for objectui#6771 when it lives on objectui#7206. Both were caught by an at-tier review rather than by the seat. The practice change, stated so it can be checked against later cards: ⭐ **every comment id this seat writes into a card or a verdict is fetched by id and its `issue_url` read in the same act** — a comment id carries no repository or issue in its digits, so an id that looks right is not a reading. ⛔ Nothing else in this card was changed; its measurement, its controls and its conclusion stand.
